column3: Attorney-at-Law  on  any  Attorney-at-Law  of  the  Supreme
Court  of  the  Democratic  Socialist  Republic  of  Sri  Lanka
has  been  in  active  practice  as  an  Instructing
Attorney for a period not less than thirty-five years
as at the date of conferring such honour;
has reached eminence in the legal profession and
has  maintained  high  standards  of  conduct  and
has not been found guilty of any criminal offence
has  not  been  found  guilty  of  any  professional
misconduct under the Supreme Court (Conduct of
and Etiquette for Attorneys-at-Law) Rules 1988 and
the provisions of the Judicature Act, No. 2 of 1978;
has been a person of good character and repute.
